documents.title: Acute Coronary Syndrome — Chest Pain Evaluation
documents.content: Suspect acute coronary syndrome in adults with acute chest pain, pressure radiating to the arm or jaw, diaphoresis, or dyspnea. Obtain a 12-lead ECG and serial troponin. Elevated troponin with ischemic symptoms supports myocardial infarction; new ST changes escalate urgency.

documents.title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia — Diagnosis
documents.content: Suspect pneumonia in adults with new cough, fever, pleuritic pain, or focal crackles plus a new infiltrate on chest radiograph. Stratify severity with CURB-65 and obtain sputum and blood cultures when admitted.

documents.title: Contact Dermatitis — Rash Management
documents.content: Contact dermatitis presents as a pruritic erythematous rash in the distribution of an allergen or irritant. Management is avoidance of the trigger and topical corticosteroids; systemic steroids are reserved for severe or widespread involvement.
